text: Runs untrusted or AI agent-generated code inside isolated Linux microVMs
quote: Run untrusted or agent-generated code in isolated Linux microVMs. Use Vercel Sandbox for agent workflows, debugging, and one-off commands.

text: Executes untrusted code (AI output, user uploads, third-party scripts) without exposing production systems
quote: Execute untrusted code safely: Run AI agent output, user uploads, or third-party scripts without exposing your production systems.

text: Can be used to build interactive tools like code playgrounds and AI-powered UI builders
quote: Build interactive tools: Create code playgrounds, AI-powered UI builders, or developer sandboxes.

text: Can run development servers with live previews
quote: Run development servers: Spin up and test applications with live previews.

text: Offers an official @vercel/sandbox SDK for JavaScript and TypeScript
quote: Use `@vercel/sandbox` for JavaScript and TypeScript

text: Authentication to the sandbox API is automatic when running on Vercel in production
quote: In production on Vercel, authentication is automatic.

text: Supports access tokens for authenticating from external CI/CD or non-Vercel environments
quote: Use access tokens when `VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN` is unavailable, such as in external CI/CD systems or non-Vercel environments.

text: Supports arbitrary Linux distributions (Ubuntu, Arch, etc.) as sandbox images, with a default image bundling Node.js LTS, Python, and coding agents
quote: Sandboxes run Linux images, with Ubuntu, Arch Linux, or any other Linux distribution you need. The default image is `vercel/sandbox/universal`, which includes the current Node.js LTS, Python 3.14, coding agents, and common utilities.

text: Can run system-privileged workloads such as container runtimes, VPN clients, and FUSE drivers
quote: System-privileged processes: Run workloads that need system-level privileges, such as container runtimes like Docker, VPN clients, and FUSE filesystem drivers.

text: Supports multi-agent isolation by giving each agent its own Linux user/home directory and shared groups for file sharing
quote: Multi-agent isolation: Give each AI agent its own Linux user with a private home directory, and share files between agents with groups.

text: Sandboxes persist state automatically on stop and resume where left off, with no manual snapshot management required
quote: Persistent sandboxes: Sandboxes that auto-save state on stop and resume where you left off. Persistence is the default. No manual snapshot management needed.

text: Supports snapshotting a running sandbox's state to resume later and skip reinstalling dependencies
quote: Snapshotting: Save the state of a running sandbox to resume later. Skip dependency installation on subsequent runs.

text: Sandboxes can be tagged with key-value pairs for categorization (environment, team, etc.)
quote: Tags: Categorize sandboxes by environment, team, or any other criteria using key-value tags.

text: Beta 'Drives' feature attaches persistent filesystem storage reusable across sandbox runs
quote: Drives (beta): Attach persistent filesystem storage to sandboxes and reuse data across sandbox runs.

text: Can mount external object stores like Amazon S3 via a FUSE driver, exposed as sandbox filesystem paths
quote: Mount remote storage: Mount an external object store such as Amazon S3 with a FUSE driver, and read and write remote files through the sandbox filesystem.

text: Lets you build custom system packages/tooling into a shared image reused across projects and teams
quote: Build your system packages and tooling into an image, and share it across projects and teams.

text: Supports creating sandboxes from custom Docker images stored in Vercel Container Registry
quote: If you already use Docker images to define your environment, store the image in Vercel Container Registry (VCR) and create the sandbox with a custom image.

text: Can retrieve an existing sandbox by name, resuming it if stopped
quote: Or retrieve an existing sandbox by name (resumes if stopped)

text: Commands can be run in blocking (wait for completion) or detached (return immediately) mode
quote: Commands can run in blocking mode (wait for completion) or detached mode (return immediately).

text: Supports streaming logs from a detached command in real time
quote: Stream logs from a detached command

text: Sandboxes can be manually stopped from the Vercel Dashboard
quote: You can also stop sandboxes from the Vercel Dashboard by navigating to Observability > Sandboxes and clicking Stop Sandbox.

text: Sandbox timeout is configurable at creation and can be extended at runtime via extendTimeout()
quote: You can configure this using the `timeout` option when creating a sandbox, and extend it using `sandbox.extendTimeout()`.

text: Sandboxes can run in multiple regions (iad1, sfo1, cle1, cdg1), selectable per sandbox or as a project default
quote: Vercel Sandbox is available in the `iad1` (default), `sfo1`, `cle1`, and `cdg1` regions. You can choose the region per sandbox or set a project default.

text: Spend Management lets you set alerts or pause projects to control sandbox costs
quote: To control costs, configure Spend Management to receive alerts or pause projects when you reach a specified amount.

text: Provides visibility into agent/user-submitted code behavior including logs, file edits, and live previews during test runs
quote: Test in isolation: Preview how user-submitted or agent-generated code behaves in a self-contained environment with access to logs, file edits, and live previews.

text: Offers an official sandbox CLI for manual testing, agentic workflows, debugging, and one-off operations
quote: Use the `sandbox` CLI for manual testing, agentic workflows, debugging, and one-off operations

text: CLI supports creating a sandbox with an explicit name
quote:
Create with an explicit name
sandbox create --name my-sandbox

text: Sandboxes can be started from Vercel Managed Images, shared/public images, or custom OCI images in Vercel Container Registry
quote: Start sandboxes from Vercel's Managed Images, a shared or public image, or your own OCI images stored in Vercel Container Registry.

text: Restoring from a snapshot is faster than a fresh sandbox because it skips reinstalling dependencies and setup steps
quote: Using a snapshot is much faster than creating from scratch because it avoids reinstalling dependencies and repeating setup steps.

text: Sandbox SDKs provide a programmatic interface to create sandboxes, run commands, and manage files
quote: The Sandbox SDKs are the recommended way to integrate Vercel Sandbox into your applications. They provide a programmatic interface to create sandboxes, run commands, and manage files.

text: Local development authentication uses `vercel link` and `vercel env pull` to obtain a dev token
quote: For local development, run `vercel link` and `vercel env pull` to get a development token. In production on Vercel, authentication is automatic.

text: Default sandbox timeout is 5 minutes, configurable and extendable
quote: The default timeout is 5 minutes. You can configure this using the `timeout` option when creating a sandbox, and extend it using `sandbox.extendTimeout()`.
